storyInfo: Twenty years ago, the Sarcophagus was sealed off to stop the Ursine Army from turning it into a weapon, yet the First Army has succeeded in firing a weapon whose power source seems to be related to the Sarcophagus.

attributes.text: In Ursine mythology, long before the Crystal Age—or perhaps a far earlier age still—
\n\nthere once lived a giant named Zheuzhyk.
The giant was so tall, the humans could not see him with their eyes. Each slight movement of his sculpted the shapes of the lands.
\n\nThe Barton Plains are the tracks of his footsteps. The endless Rudokny Mountains were just barely enough to serve as a pillow when he slumbered.
\n\nThe giant in the legends could not definitively be described as good or evil. He was simply a big, simple existence that the masses below could look up to.
What is difficult to explain, however, is that references to gigantic beings like Zheuzhyk are often found in different mythologies across the land.
\n\nThese similar stories might perhaps reflect a common characteristic in all human subconscious:
\n\nNo matter when and where, from the bottom of their hearts, humans seek some kind of a greater power—an enormous being, abstract or specific, that stands in contrast to their minuscule existence.
Mankind is accustomed to worshipping great beings conjured in the imagination, and seeking their projections in reality.
\n\nYet when such a being finally presents itself before the masses in some shape and form—
\n\nIt never fails to crush their genial fantasies.

attributes.content: You know, Boris really is a nutjob.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: You saw his arrogant shit face when he met the Marshal too, didn't you? He made a bit of coin these past few years and it gave him a big head.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Get him a few more coins and he won't even bow to the tsar.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: He figures the Marshal doesn't have the balls to try anything funny. Hell, if the Marshal can't scrape together a decent price? He'd probably turn around right there and side with the Third Army instead.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: Heh, that's how anyone would play it, with a decent way out.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: A short-sighted businessman sitting on a treasure like this is only ever gonna think about how to use it to fill his pockets. He's never given a single thought to its true worth!
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: No wonder he doesn't give the Ursine military the respect we deserve. He can't understand what our land is built on. Really, nobody gives us our due respect!
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: If I were the Marshal, I would've slit that coward's throat and stamped my fingerprint on the contract in his blood.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Heh, if I were the Marshal... I'd order the army to fight to the end, until every Ursine learned to respect us. Not like now... with everyone looking down on us.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Gah... enough of that nonsense!
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: Do you seriously think the Marshal ever actually backed those morons in the Sixth and Eighth Armies?
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: With everything they've been up to? They were destined to fail. One does not simply provoke a rebellion in Ursus, especially not with so few guns and battleships... or even with ten times what they had.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: They're no different from any of those businessmen. They don't even know where Ursine pride comes from—but the Marshal had it figured out long ago.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: So count yourself lucky. You still get to grumble while you're out on a mission, instead of being sent to the Far North to turn to stone with the Infected.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: The hell are you doing?
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: What I was ordered to do. Making sure everyone's dead.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: We could've at least had him find the others!
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Let's not waste more time. We wouldn't even be here today if these white coat bastards had half a mind to cooperate.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: There, found one. Hiding under the desk there.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: No! No! Let me go!
attributes.name: Extremely Frightened Voice

attributes.content: Please! Please don't kill me! I'll tell you whatever you want—
attributes.name: Extremely Frightened Voice

attributes.content: What do we do? He's willing to cooperate.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Trust me. It'll be faster if we just do this ourselves.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: Keep looking. There has to be more of them.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: And get a head count. Remember. No one gets out of this place alive.
attributes.name: Impatient Voice

attributes.content: I'm starting to get a little annoyed too. This place hardly has any ventilation, and it reeks of blood. Ugh, it's getting my boots all sticky.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: Oh... Found one.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.content: There's another here.
attributes.name: Unhappy Voice

attributes.text: An ancient Minoan philosopher once said that 'Man is, by nature, a creative animal.'
\n\nBy his works, man accumulates experience he then uses to create—in concrete or abstract—and solve the problems he faces.
Such creations fulfill man's needs and assuage his fears. At the same time, they reflect his aesthetics and morals.
\n\nEach and every one of mankind's creations is a manifestation of its own traits—
\n\nPerhaps it was the same process by which the Creator created mankind.
And among all of mankind's creations, the one that best reflects its innate nature, for good or for evil—
\n\nThe concept of the 'nation' undoubtedly takes the crown.

attributes.content: Director! They've made it into Area D!
attributes.name: Timid Researcher

attributes.content: I heard... the sound of fighting... Are they... are they killing people?
attributes.name: Timid Researcher

attributes.content: Ilia, how much longer?
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Forty minutes.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: We've done all we can, but it'll take forty more minutes to complete the lockdown procedure.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Do we really have to wait till it's completely locked down?
attributes.name: Timid Researcher

attributes.content: What else can we do?! Do you want me to hand this thing over to the army completely intact, and let it fall into the butchers' hands, letting them effortlessly massacre even more people?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Blyat! I've lived my whole life as a failure. I refuse to be an accomplice to these murderers even in death!
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: It's too late...
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: But how could the butchers work out all our secrets so quickly...?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: We have a traitor in our midst... Director, somebody must've sold us out.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Sergei, maybe? I should've known when he kept probing me with all those questions.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Blyat! It must be him... Why? He could have been a good man...
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Calm down, Ilia. Thinking like this will not do us any good right now.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Focus on the task at hand. We still have a chance to salvage something.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Director... It's too late for us... isn't it?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: You got my warning. You shouldn't have come back. Even with you here, we still won't finish in—
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Ilia, take the others and go.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Go? Where could we possibly go?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: To Taymyr, in the north. It's close to the Third Army's territory. Andrian wouldn't dare launch a manhunt there.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Hide there and stay far away from the cities. Avoid contact with any factions of the government, and do not believe any promises of protection the Third Army gives you.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Go now. I will stay.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Ilia?
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: No... I will stay behind.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Ilia.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: I won't run. I can't. You shouldn't be entrusting our colleagues' lives to a man like me!
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Director Kal'tsit... No, my teacher. The land needs you far more than it needs me. You should go, not me. You should never have come back at all!
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Even if you find a way to hide the Originium on your skin, they will find out that you're Infected. Then you will suffer a fate a hundred times worse than a quick and easy death—
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Besides, only you can lead our innocent colleagues to safety. You can't say no.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: But you, too, have a reason to live... Think about Lyudmila, your daughter—
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: Please, care for her.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Take her away from here, away from this country, and as far away as you can... Heh, I was hoping she would get to study under you for much longer, but it is what it is.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Don't tell her what happened here today. Nothing good will come of it. Let her explore the land in her own way.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: I promise you. I will take her far away from Ursus. Until she is able to care for herself, she will be safe.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: And I promise you this. You and your colleagues' work will not go to waste.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: That's more than enough for me...
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: ...It's an intriguing thought. We chose to open this Sarcophagus before, and now we choose to keep it dormant. Which was the right choice?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: We did what we thought to be correct. As for the answer, perhaps it is up to Lyudmila... or even her children to determine.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: I guess you're right... Now go.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Goodbye, Ilia.
attributes.name: Kal'tsit

attributes.content: So you're the last one?
attributes.name: Fourth Army Soldier

attributes.content: The last what?
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: The last one alive in the lab? Yes. The last one in this country to despise its savagery? Somehow, I doubt it.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: You stayed behind. What did you do to the Sarcophagus?
attributes.name: Fourth Army Soldier

attributes.content: Oh, about ten seconds ago, the Sarcophagus's core function completely locked down. You want to reactivate it? It'll take you lot a century.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: You—what are you, vanguards of the murderous Fourth Army? Go back and tell Andrian that his plans to use this beast as a weapon of territorial expansion have just gone belly-up.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Too bad, the glorious Marshal Andrian has failed again and again. His army couldn't conquer a tiny laboratory, or, hell, even a lone, miserable researcher.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Alright, you may exercise your authority to take my life now.
attributes.name: Ilia

attributes.content: Hm, not bad, for a hard-headed shit...
attributes.name: Fourth Army Soldier

attributes.content: We'll do it your way.
attributes.name: Fourth Army Soldier

attributes.text: For the Empire of Ursus, or perhaps even for all the lands, the Sarcophagus was a groundbreaking discovery, possibly meant for a different era.
\n\nI, too, once had ill-timed expectations for it. The tragedy that unfolded before my eyes, in the end, was my punishment.
The innocent sacrifice of the talented researchers in the institute...
\n\nNo doubt that was a punishment to this country for its hubris.
\n\nEven if the effects of this punishment may not be fully realized until much, much later.
In this moment of time, I can offer only a small piece of advice.
\n\nIf you no longer wish to be dragged into this endless cycle of political conflict and revenge...
\n\nIf you believe that there yet remains something precious on these lands worth protecting from the mandibles of the manglerbeasts—
\n\nThen I ask you to keep this letter and to stop the armies' pursuit of the laboratory's survivors.
This is neither a threat nor a plea.
\n\nI simply hope that you will make the right decision based on your interests and conscience.
To Marquess Sheremetyevo Boris
In 1077, a bloody incident occurred in the southeastern corner of Ursus. For an empire that had just suffered a devastating civil war, it was hardly a noticeable incident.

Perhaps it will take a hundred years—when historians revisit these turbulent times in their piles of old writings—for everyone to truly understand that what happened at the research institute in Chernobog was both emblematic of its era and a seed.
Even if, at this moment in time, it is buried deep under the Ursine permafrost, waiting for its time to sprout.

attributes.content: Where am I?
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: What happened to the court martial? What happened to due process?
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: Why did you bring me here? And where are my men?
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: Shut up.
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: You would have to kill me.
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: You're on death row. It doesn't make a difference whether we kill you now or later.
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: Too bad for you, the bigwigs don't have time to deal with seditious leadership like yourself, so...
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: You'll just have to hold up here. Listen to how your men in the other rooms stay quiet?
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: I'm a soldier, not a criminal. The same goes for my men!
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: From the moment you worked up the arrogance to rise against the Marshal, your entire formation ceased to be a part of the glorious Fourth Army.
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: I did the right thing, and all the warriors you have dismissed as traitors, and in fact all Ursines of conscience, know that this is the right thing to do.
attributes.name: Young Voice

attributes.content: No, Captain Yakov Petrov.
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: What you did was the foolish thing to do, and you dragged your family and your friends into this mess.
attributes.name: Grumpy Voice

attributes.content: Mother, please, sit down first... You're shaking.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The people from the army have already gone.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Army... Yakov...
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Is that you, Yakov?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: You are back?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: But the apple trees have yet to blossom... It's too soon for your summer vacation.
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Has Marshal Andrian been treating you well? Has he been bringing you on his adventures? What about the clothes I had them bring to you? Did they fit?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: I can't see well, so I couldn't sew your name onto them... but Sofia helped. You've always loved her handicrafts—
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Sofia?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Mother.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: You're not Sofia.
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Nor am I Yakov. I am neither Brother nor Sister.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Who are you? Why are you in my home? Somebody—
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Mother, I'm Tulin, your young son who has been away for a long time. You remember me, do you not?
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The servants have been dismissed, and the butler has left.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: What are you saying?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: Yakov is in prison. Sofia is married, but she is busy scrambling about in Deity Grypherburg, desperately trying to get him out. She needs money to resolve some issues, and we must help.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Moreover, we cannot embroil the innocent in a fate they do not deserve, can we?
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: *sigh...*
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: No matter the case, please listen to what I have to say, Mother. You may never have heard these things, but this letter was written by Yakov in prison.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Let me read it for you...
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The boy says and opens the envelope, only to find a blank sheet of paper.
In an instant, his face turns as white as the sheet in his hands.
Yakov... Isn't Yakov in the army?
attributes.name: Dazed Woman

attributes.content: The army has been here, Mother.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The boy folds the sheet of paper in half, bit by bit, as if needing the time to slow down and process the truth.
Then, he puts the small and neatly folded square into his breast pocket, normally occupied by a handkerchief, to keep it close to his heart.
They said that because of the role that Yakov played in the Fourth Army's mutiny...
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The Petrovs have been stripped of nobility and are now mere commoners... to be exiled to the Northern Tundra Mines, Mining Zone No. 9.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: We set out tomorrow.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Old Peter's buried. It's time for us to go.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: First, it was our children, then our wives, and then our parents... How many more bodies will we have to bury?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: What are you doing, writing a letter? Is it to your mother?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: No... Not a letter. I'm just trying to put everything I see into words. If the chance ever comes, I hope people will come to know all that has happened.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: You still have the strength for that? I must say, I really envy you.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: I can't walk very far, and we still have yet to make it to the Northern Tundra.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: It's only been three months since we left Omska.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: It'll probably be spring again by the time we make it to the mines.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Spring... Haha! Spring!
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: My sweet summer child. You think there is spring in the tundra...?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: Right, spring. As long as we make it there.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: Your mother was spared because she's blind and off her rocker.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: She doesn't have to suffer the pain of exile, and you are spared from having to bury her like a nameless woman. Thanks to that, you are so optimistic, you might as well be a lunatic.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: But... what gives you the right?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: What gives you the right?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: You, too, are an exiled criminal, and yet someone like you gets special treatment. You don't have to watch as every member of your family slowly takes their last breaths, as their bodies slowly turn cold.
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: Is it because I was only a dime-a-dozen porter before I turned into an Infected?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: What did I do wrong? And what did you do right?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: The Infected murmurs. He wants to scream the thoughts in his mind out loud more than anybody, but he is trapped under the watchful gaze of the guards.
The boy shakes his head and moves up closer toward the Infected.
I was privileged, yes... And it wasn't because of my own hard work. For that, I feel ashamed.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: But the question you posed is one that I am seeking the answer to myself.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: What?
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: Why are some of us born privileged, while others are born disdained? Why do we stand in opposition to each other, even though we are all humans? What can we do to break free of the status quo?
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: I will tell you. I don't know.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: But my instinct tells me that we need to at least survive and stand back up.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: It's only when we stand together and combine our strength that we are able to keep thinking about where the problem lies and figure out a way to change something.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: What are you talking about—
attributes.name: Despairing Infected

attributes.content: The boy suddenly lifts his head and looks into the Infected man's perplexed eyes.
Just pretend I'm talking nonsense.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: The way I see it, people like you with nothing to their name are the true masters of the land.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.content: For the time being, please, climb onto my back. At the very least, I still have some strength in me. I can carry you for a while.
attributes.name: Quiet Boy

attributes.text: '...In Iberia, people almost never turn their gazes upon one another, as if making eye contact were sinful, and as if doing so would violate a deeply held creed.
'I have also witnessed similar behaviors in the mines of Ursus, the slums of Leithanien, and the underground factories of Victoria.

'At first, I surmised that they feared seeing in their soot-covered faces the same despair they felt in their hearts. It was only later that I realized it was because, their eyes had little room for anything beyond the urgency of survival.

'That being the case, who could blame them for their silence and for failing to notice their fellow man, for failing to look to a future even further away, for failing to stand together to rise against their oppressors?'

'The land sprawls far and wide. I traveled throughout Ursus, and then made my way to even farther lands. On my way, I continued to tell those who had lost everything—or perhaps have never truly had anything: You are the true masters of the land.

'As things currently stand, and we have yet to see any real change, my words feel like little more than mockery, yet I need to keep telling them. It is only by planting these seeds that they may subconsciously realize the truth behind my words and let them sprout within their hearts.
'When one truly has nothing, one has nothing to lose, granting the most resolute of resolves. The same truth lies within us all.'

attributes.content: Boss!
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: We're all packed up, ready to go. How about you?
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Hm...
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Boss?
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Uh... Oh! Right. Let's get going.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Thanks for coming to get me. I'm all packed up too—
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Uhh.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: You dug out all this stuff again? What a mess... Here, I'll help you pack up.
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Thanks!
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: I came to the mines late, I've never seen the one who sent you the letters. Did they really leave the mines and keep on writing to you?
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Yes.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: First time I've ever heard of anyone missing life in the mines so much.
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Perhaps it's not the mines that he misses, but the people.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: As I remember, when the news of political prisoners getting pardoned first got here to the Northern Tundra, his first reaction wasn't one of joy. It was worry.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: He was worried that we wouldn't be able to leave like him, and that his theories would never be proven...
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: But he still left in the end.
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Of course. He said he'd travel all across Ursus, and now we're leaving this place behind too, aren't we?
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Then let's get going, Boss.
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Right, I started calling you 'Boss' because that's what everyone here calls you, but I've been thinking, you've got to have an actual name, right?
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Huh, have I really never told you?
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Hm... Tulin. You can call me Tulin.
attributes.name: The Pensive Youth

attributes.content: Hell yeah, 'Tulin.' Good name. Here, I'll help you up.
attributes.name: Nimble Miner

attributes.content: Thank you...
attributes.name: Tulin

attributes.content: Yeah, let's hurry and get out of here.
attributes.name: Tulin

attributes.content: While the snow is still calm, and before the ones in the warm houses change their minds.
attributes.name: Tulin

attributes.text: '...Investigation shows that the extremely provocative messages left behind by the instigators are all quotations from Yakov Petrov, a war criminal who got what he deserved during the Great Rebellion.
'While on death row, he wrote a will...'
'Whose fault was the Katorga Uprising? What should we do now? How do we save these young people who know nothing but rebellion?'
'While the Chairman's condition is now stable, the fiend behind the assassination attempt remains at large.
'The Deity Grypherburg Police call on everyone to stay indoors after nightfall to avoid arousing suspicion and interfering with the search operation.'

attributes.content: (Flips through the newspaper)
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: (Closes the newspaper)
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: Zdravstvuyte, gospodin. Could you fetch me a fresher newspaper?
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: Uh. I-I'm afraid that will require prior approval.
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: This lounge's newspapers and reading material are maintained daily by a page. I can't just conjure up one out of thin air for you.
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: Besides, you are an Infected. You may have been let in, but I don't know if you really have authorization to read this—
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: *cough*!
attributes.name: Hasty Noble

attributes.content: Gospodin Gorchikov—I mean, General!
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: You may call me Vice Chairman here. Thank you for your help. I will handle the rest.
attributes.name: Hasty Noble

attributes.content: What? Could that be... is this your guest?
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: Bozhe moy... I'm so stupid! Please accept my sincerest apologies, gospodin, for my words—
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: So it goes. What you said is the truth.
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: Indeed, I am an Infected.
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: The newspaper. You, I... I—
attributes.name: Nervous Servant

attributes.content: *sigh...* Just do as I said, and let me handle the rest!
attributes.name: Hasty Noble

attributes.content: 'General?'
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: Please, don't tease me... You know better than anyone whether or not I will become general.
attributes.name: Hasty Noble

attributes.content: You weren't so hard on yourself before, Vasily.
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: And you weren't this easy to talk to, for an officer of the army.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: The man who stands before you now is a mere Infected warrior, no longer an Imperial Guard instructor.
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: You still remember my name, do you not? Call me Hellagur.
attributes.name: Solemn Soldier

attributes.content: Very good, Gospodin Hellagur. How does it feel to return to Grypherburg? This is hardly a time for sightseeing, but still.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: It's a lot quieter than I expected. A lot of things have changed, so much so that hardly anything from times gone by still remains.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Right. So much has changed, and who could say whether these changes are for the better or worse?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: The businessmen have gotten richer. Thanks to that, the city has become a more beautiful place. At the same time, modesty and all our other virtues are now valued less.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Perhaps you've heard already. His Imperial Majesty is going to build a so-called 'citizens' forum' and hand over all decision-making to the common folk of Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: And now, we can all say that the nobles have finally given up on the one job they still had and handed it over to the commoners.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: It sounds like you don't agree with this at all.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: It's not up to me to agree or disagree, but if there's someone out there who can solve all these problems facing society, it doesn't matter who that person is.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: This doesn't sound like something the vice chairman, with all his authority, would say.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: I've never been one eager to put my power on full display. You know that better than anyone.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Come to think of it, I'm surprised they didn't confiscate your blade when you entered the city.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Oh, this. All they did was make a note of it. I didn't receive too much... special treatment. This is only a replica, and one that hasn't been sharpened. It's as lethal as a piece of scrap metal. Perhaps that's why.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Where's the real one?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: I gave it to someone I trust.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Someone you trust...
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: I understand you have a daughter.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Yes, I do. If we find the time later, I would love to introduce you to her. She has heard many stories of your achievements, and she respects you deeply.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: And it's not just her. Many in today's Imperial Guard still remember your name.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: It's been some years since we hung up our hats, but those stories yet fly over the Imperial Guard Academy like a banner. At your convenience, I'd like to take you for a visit.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: You have my thanks for keeping those sacrifices so close to your heart, but I truly have no intention of serving as a banner ever again.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: I am here for another reason. Surely you must already know that Rhodes Island has established an office here in Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: I am well aware. I even signed a few documents in the Chairman's stead.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: *sigh...* Even if our stance on the Infected has relaxed, the conflicts regarding them remain as sharp as ever.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Still, if we're speaking of you personally—I would be happy to take this chance to restore your honors in Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: I don't need the empire to restore my identity or honor.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Then what do you need?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Simply put, what Rhodes Island needs is precisely what I need.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: More specifically, you mean—
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: 'Please inform Chairman Witte that the designated Rhodes Islanders have departed for Deity Grypherburg.'
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: If my timing is right, they should have already made it to the office.
attributes.name: Hellagur

attributes.content: Oh...
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: Chairman—
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: Is the Chairman here?!
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: I am the vice chairman. What's the matter?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: I... I have a report!
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: Th-The First Army—
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: The soldier tries his best to get a noun out of his mouth, but he finds himself frozen when he spots Hellagur standing to the side.
Vasily shakes his head to signal that there is nothing to worry about.
What of the First Army?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: The new weapon of mass destruction that the First Army has been developing... The firing test was successful!
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: And, what's the problem?
attributes.name: Vasily

attributes.content: The problem is... the weapon doesn't use Originium... or any energy source that we've ever employed!
attributes.name: Nervous Soldier

attributes.content: What?
attributes.name: Vasily
